issues.title: Are cfg/algo/mappo.yaml defaults + 600M frames enough to reproduce the paper MAPPO baseline? Dist-reward coefficient seems too small — sanity check?
issues.body:
Hi, thanks for the paper and the open release.

We're trying to reproduce the MAPPO baseline on top of this repo
(`train.py` + `algo=mappo` + `task=HideAndSeek`), at HEAD of master
(last upstream push 2025-05-15). Setup matches the README:
Isaac Sim 2022.2.0, default `HideAndSeek.yaml` (use_eval=1,
scenario_flag='wall', catch_radius=0.3, dist_reward_coef=1.0,
catch_reward_coef=60.0, collision_coef=100.0, etc.),
`cfg/algo/mappo.yaml` at its current defaults. The only change we
made was raising `task.env.num_envs` from `100` to `2048`.

Training: ~600M frames. Eval: the pursuers basically don't pursue
— no meaningful closing-distance behavior, capture rate essentially
zero across the standard eval scenarios. We don't see the table
numbers.

Before we keep tweaking on our side, two sanity checks:

1. Are the values currently in `cfg/algo/mappo.yaml` the same
   ones you used to produce the MAPPO row in Table II of
   arXiv:2409.15866? If they drifted from the paper baseline,
   is there a tag / commit / config file that pins the
   paper hyperparameters?

2. `dist_reward_coef=1.0` looks quite small compared to
   `catch_reward_coef=60.0` and `collision_coef=100.0`. Did you
   ever need to raise `dist_reward_coef` (or a dense approach
   term) to actually get closing-distance pressure to emerge in
   practice? Or should 600M frames + 2048 envs be plenty and
   we're missing something else?

Thanks — pointing us at the right baseline config would save us
a lot of trial-and-error.

issues.body:
Hi — thanks for this repo and the helpful instructions.

I downloaded the isaac_sim-2022.2.0 .zip you shared, but it looks like the package is the Linux build (contains many .sh scripts and no Windows executables). I am using a Windows laptop with RTX 5060 and would like to run your project natively on Windows.

If a Windows package is not available, would you recommend a specific Isaac Sim version (Windows) that is known to work with your code?

issues.title: Inquiry regarding missing pre-trained weights, default_environment.usd, and real-world deployment scripts
issues.body:
First of all, thank you very much for sharing your excellent work and open-sourcing the code for OPEN! I have been reading your recent paper "Online Planning for Multi-UAV Pursuit-Evasion in Unknown Environments Using Deep Reinforcement Learning," and I find the CTBR control and prediction-enhanced MARL methodology truly inspiring.

I am currently trying to reproduce your simulation results and potentially deploy the policy on our quadrotors, but I encountered a few missing components in the repository. I would greatly appreciate your help with the following:

1. Pre-trained Checkpoints: I noticed that the repository currently does not include any pre-trained model weights (e.g., the .pt files). Because training the MAPPO policy for 2 billion timesteps requires significant computational resources and time, could you kindly provide a pre-trained checkpoint? Having the weights would be incredibly helpful for the community to quickly test and evaluate the algorithm using eval.py
2. Missing default_environment.usd: When running the training and evaluation scripts, I noticed that cfg/train.yaml has the parameter use_local_usd: true, which attempts to load default_environment.usd. However, this file seems to be missing from the repository, causing Isaac Sim to render a completely unlit, white screen in headless mode. I managed to temporarily fix this by setting it to false, but it would be great if you could upload the missing custom scene file for completeness.
3. Real-World Deployment Code: In Section V.F of your paper, you demonstrated an impressive Zero-Shot transfer to real Crazyflie quadrotors using a motion capture system. However, I couldn't find the deployment scripts (e.g., the Vicon/OptiTrack state receiver and the radio communication node for CTBR commands) in the current codebase. Do you have any plans to release the real-world deployment scripts in the future?

Thank you again for your time and for contributing such a high-quality RL framework to the UAV community. Looking forward to your reply!

Best regards.

issues.title: Third Party Packages and isaac_Sim-2022.2.0 errors
issues.body:
Hi. I found the "git submodule update -- init -- recursive" in "3.Third Party Packages" will report an error, indicating that torchrl and tensordict cannot be installed. I checked and it seems that the author from Omnidrones deleted the relevant libraries, which caused the installation to fail according to the instructions in README.

In addition, there are many bugs in the isaac_Sim-2022.2.0 version, including loading .so files and missing a large number of key library paths. I am wondering if you have also fixed this isaac sim version yourself. May I ask if you will continue to use isaac_Sim 2022.2.0 for updates in the future? If I use Omnidrones, I can only use this version?

We do not need the Omniverse.

1. Sorry, but I am no longer maintaining this repository, and the pretrained checkpoint has not been preserved. However, the checkpoint can be reproduced easily using the current codebase. Our training was conducted on two NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPUs, and the full training process takes about 15 hours of wall-clock time. If your goal is simply to verify the checkpoint’s performance in simulation while minimizing training cost, you can directly set smoothness_coef = 0. Furthermore, if you want to validate the results as quickly as possible, you can initialize the task with a single fixed scenario and intentionally overfit to it. For example, you may randomize only the initial positions of the drones and the evader, while setting the scene to "wall".

In addition, I added a safety check before evaluation to avoid potential issues caused by the two drones being initialized too close to each other. However, this did not lead to any noticeable improvement.

If you have successfully reproduced the reported results, would you mind sharing your experimental setup or any details about your reproduction process? At the moment, I am not sure whether the issue is simply that 30 million training frames are still insufficient, or whether there might be something wrong with my configuration, training pipeline, or evaluation procedure.

Any suggestions or insights would be greatly appreciated. Thanks!

1. Please refer to Figure 8 in the paper. It takes nearly 1e9 timesteps to achieve a success rate of approximately 35%. When using MAPPO alone, about 1.5e9 timesteps are required before the success rate becomes greater than zero. 2. For easier debugging, you can increase catch_radius so that the UAVs can catch the evader more easily. This allows you to quickly observe an increase in reward and visually verify that the agents have learned a capture strategy.
